solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game spirit shown by one booed on stage endlessly?

parts.note: the ka is the spiritual double or soul in ancient Egyptian belief

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a baddie is the villain the pantomime audience boos

explanation.surface: A sporting spirit displayed by a pantomime villain who never stops being jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: KA is the Egyptian soul; a pantomime is a British Christmas stage show where the audience boos the baddie.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabaddi is a South Asian contact team sport, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Start packing up before the end

indicators.note: before the end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up, as is packing it up

explanation.surface: Begin putting things away just before finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick in is to begin taking effect, as a drug or a rule does.

clue.text: Daring US agent like a baby sometimes?

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
a fed is an FBI agent in American slang

explanation.surface: A bold American agent acting like an infant now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve, as in losing your bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Many infants are nourished from a bottle rather than at the breast, hence sometimes.

clue.text: Claimed to be mistreated: one has a point!

indicators.note: mistreated suggests rough handling, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protesting ill treatment insists they are right.
explanation.walkthrough: Has a point looks like making a valid argument, but it is the dot in a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal fraction is written with a point separating whole units from tenths.

clue.text: One's packed stylish, plain, overnight case

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: packed means the one is stuffed into the plain word

parts.note: patent means obvious or plain to see
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a smart, simple overnight bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Case is a medical case, a hospital patient, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: An inpatient is someone admitted to hospital who stays at least one night.

clue.text: Fresh cigars initially taken from breadbasket

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word taken

parts.note: first letter only

explanation.surface: New cigars, first sampled, have been removed from a bread basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Breadbasket is slang for the stomach, so the definition is adjectival: coming from the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach, which slang calls the breadbasket.

clue.text: River and Asian peak gone over by travel writer

indicators.note: in a down entry, gone over by puts the travel word on top of the river and the peak

parts.note: to go is to travel
K1, also called Masherbrum, is a peak in the Karakoram; the digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A travel writer has covered a river and an Asian mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Travel writer looks like one phrase, but travel is wordplay and writer alone is the definition. K1 is the Karakoram peak, with 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorki (also spelt Gorky) was a Russian novelist and playwright, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Small toy, one that hums?

parts.note: to tinker is to toy or fiddle with something

explanation.surface: A tiny plaything that buzzes to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Hums is British slang for smells bad, not singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is something that smells foul, and to hum is slang for giving off a bad smell.

clue.text: One who's "dreaded" retiring, beats a retreat to downsize

indicators.note: retiring means that part is read going backwards
to downsize means take only a small part of the words beats a retreat

parts.note: the letters are inside these words

explanation.surface: A feared person withdrawing, beating a retreat to scale back.
explanation.walkthrough: Dreaded is in quotes because it means wearing dreadlocks, not feared.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians commonly wear their hair in dreadlocks, so a Rasta is often dreadlocked.

clue.text: Seed quietly snaffled by smart parrot

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart

indicators.note: snaffled by means the quiet letter is grabbed inside the parrot

parts.note: the kea is a New Zealand parrot
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A seed silently grabbed by a clever parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is the edible seed of a leguminous plant, used in hummus.

clue.text: Copper with black coat and cloak placed inside skip

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: placed inside tells us the cloak goes within the black coat

parts.note: tar is a black coating, as on roads
a cape is a sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: A police officer with a dark coat and a cloak stuffed into a rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman and skip like a rubbish container, but copper is the metal and skip is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a caper is to leap or frolic about, which is what skipping does.

clue.text: Get away with a summit, regularly cancelled, being put back

indicators.note: put back means the kept letters are read in reverse order
regularly cancelled means every other letter is struck out, keeping the alternate ones

parts.note: the letters remaining after every other one goes

explanation.surface: Escaping with a mountain top, regularly called off and postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of the three words, then read them backwards. IMSHI is old army slang picked up in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Imshi is a slang command telling someone to clear off, the same as the exclamation get away.

clue.text: Current success at cards generating belief

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a slam is winning all or all but one of the tricks at bridge

explanation.surface: A run of winning at the card table producing confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is a religious faith, and a faith is a belief system.

clue.text: Research group's rare function embraced by thousands

parts.note: rare air is thin air

indicators.note: embraced by means the function sits inside the two thousands

parts.note: K for a thousand, twice for the plural
tan is the trigonometric tangent function

explanation.surface: A research team's unusual role is supported by thousands of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Function is the trigonometric one, tangent, abbreviated TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A think tank is an organisation of experts that researches policy questions.

clue.text: Fine old stories presented by composer before cabaret

parts.note: a story can be a lie, as when a child tells stories
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Good old tales performed by a composer ahead of a cabaret show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Folies Bergère is a famous Paris music hall known for its cabaret revues.

clue.text: Porter, say, coming across well time after time, making splash

indicators.note: coming across means the beer spans and encloses the rest

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of the drink
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: A railway porter crossing a well again and again, splashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a railway worker, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespatter is to spray with drops of liquid or mud, much as to splash does.

clue.text: Phoned in, somehow having obtained right number

indicators.note: somehow says the letters fall into some other order
having obtained means the extra letter is added to the mix

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called in after somehow getting the correct phone number.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is read as numb-er, something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are the body's natural painkillers, which deaden pain as a numbing agent does.

clue.text: Mix two books up with film about bird racing machines

indicators.note: mixed up means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
B for book, twice
Kes is a 1969 British film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: Jumbling a couple of books along with a nature film about racing birds.
explanation.definitionFit: BMX bikes are small sturdy bicycles built for dirt-track racing and stunts.

clue.text: A museum's data, strangely, ultimately ignored one's founder

definitions.text: A museum's data, strangely, ultimately ignored one's founder

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put into an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of ignored

parts.note: last letter only

explanation.surface: A museum's records oddly overlook the person who started it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the museum is the waxworks, and its founder's name comes from rearranging the museum's own data.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Tussaud founded the London waxworks museum that still bears her name.

clue.text: Press over the moon, meeting with new cardinal

indicators.note: over places the press above the moon in this down entry

parts.note: a mill is a press for grinding or crushing
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Journalists ecstatic about a newly appointed cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal looks like a churchman, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal number is a counting number such as a thousand thousand.

clue.text: Reveals fresh embarrassment for golfer?

parts.note: to air views is to reveal them
hot means just made or fresh, as in hot news

explanation.surface: A golfer's new humiliation is laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: An air shot is a swing that misses the ball completely, a mortifying moment on the course.

clue.text: Agitation after leading pair's decamped, note, a catalyst

indicators.note: the leading pair decamping means the first two letters leave

parts.note: a frenzy is a state of wild agitation
me is a variant of mi, the third note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Turmoil once the front two have gone, note, sparks change.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds up a biochemical reaction, i.e. a biological catalyst.

clue.text: One requiring pluck (bravo!), like a dog in space

parts.note: B is Bravo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a la means in the manner of, so like
Laika was the Soviet dog sent into orbit in 1957

explanation.surface: Someone who needs courage, cheered on, rather like a dog sent into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluck looks like courage, but it means plucking strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A balalaika is a Russian stringed instrument played by plucking its strings.

clue.text: Wool cap for priest needing to be stretched?

indicators.note: stretched means the priest's word is made longer by doubling its opening letter, the cap for priest

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest
the cap of the priest's word is its first letter, repeated here so the top letter becomes double

explanation.surface: A woollen hat for a cleric that will need stretching to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The cap for priest is the opening letter of the priest's own name, doubled to stretch the word by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Llama is the soft fibre shorn from the South American animal, and cloth made from it.

clue.text: One fag end's left unpleasant discharge

indicators.note: the end leaving means the last letter goes

parts.note: fag is British slang for a tiresome job, a chore

explanation.surface: A single cigarette butt left behind gives off something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag looks like a cigarette, but it is British slang for a tedious task.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is a thin watery fluid oozing from a wound or ulcer.

clue.text: Concerned with split in stage, not for the first time

definitions.text: stage, not for the first time

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letter headings
a run is a split or ladder in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: Worried about a rift in a theatrical production that has been seen before.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage is a verb here: to stage a show again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun something is to put it on again, as with a repeated broadcast or race.

clue.text: This military don sounded out transport solution

indicators.note: sounded out means the answer is said like the phrase, in British speech

parts.note: a car key is what solves the problem of starting your transport

explanation.surface: A military academic voicing a solution to a transport problem.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the answer sounds like car key. Don is the verb, to put on, not a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the drab cloth of army uniforms, so it is what the military puts on.

clue.text: After success briefly had opening they retire

indicators.note: after tells us the rest follows the success

parts.note: a hit is a successful song or show

indicators.note: had opening they means the shortened word splits they apart and sits inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means the word had loses its last letter

parts.note: the word had, which briefly cuts short

explanation.surface: Following a win, someone had a gap before they withdrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the hay is a casual idiom for going to bed, just as retire can mean.

clue.text: One maybe coming across interference in works?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that spans a gap, like a bridge
second meaning: from the idiom a ... in the works, meaning sabotage

explanation.walkthrough: One meaning is literal, a thing that spans; the other leans on the idiom of throwing a spanner in the works.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a wrench, and the idiom a spanner in the works means something that disrupts a plan.

clue.text: Train transporting article for universal visual aids

indicators.note: transporting means the train carries the article in its body, in place of something else
for means the article takes the place of the letter for universal

parts.note: a retinue is a train of attendants following a dignitary
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A train carrying an item intended for general use.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the film-classification letter for universal. Swap it for A in the word for an entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: The retinae are the light-sensitive layers at the back of the eyes, essential organs of sight.
